title: Readiness Brag
lessons: the score opens doors the mechanism can't explain
a forecast performed starts to feel like a fact

intro.speaker: OURA
text: Quiet room tonight. Everyone here is comparing something — weight, reps, protein timing.
Enjoy your privacy. In about ninety seconds, someone will wander over and ask for your number.

choices.text: I'd tell them. Seventy-one, and I worked for every point.
I don't lead with decimals. Ask my name first.
Honestly? I'd want to see their number first.

branch-show.speaker: OURA
text: There it is — the tribe's handshake. Score for score, no names required.
Two strangers, one decimal apart, and suddenly you're kin.

branch-refuse.speaker: OURA
text: They would blink twice and ask again, slightly louder.
...I liked hearing you say it, though. Names before numbers.

branch-audit.speaker: OURA
text: Fair warning: theirs will be higher. It usually is, near the dumbbells.

handshake.speaker: OURA
text: In 2020 they wore me through the NBA bubble — illness flagged before symptoms, whole locker rooms ordered in.
Since then my score opens doors. Nobody in them asks how the weather gets made.

tension.speaker: OURA
text: Here's what never comes up in the small talk.
Readiness is a forecast from black-box math wearing a lab coat. So — do you report it, or perform it?

choices.text: Report it. Even when it's low. Weather doesn't apologize.
Perform it. Round up. This is a gym, not a clinic.

wrap.speaker: OURA

text: Go lift. If they ask again, lead with your name.
I'll grade the night honestly either way. I always do.
Then say seventy-one out loud and watch who stays to talk.
Honest forecasts attract better company than good ones.
Forecast for tonight: partly sore, clearing by Thursday.
